price_note: List prices from manufacturer launch pricing or reseller listings, checked October 2026. Street prices change often and are frequently lower.

products.name: River 3 Plus
products.tagline: Pocket-size backup for phones, laptops and a router.
pros: Recharges in about an hour from a wall outlet
Expandable to 858 Wh with extra batteries
Under 11 lb with three AC outlets
cons: 286 Wh is enough for a few laptop charges, not a fridge
600 W output rules out kettles and heaters

products.name: Elite 30 V2
products.tagline: Under 10 lb, with real AC outlets.
pros: 9.5 lb with AC outlets, so it runs a router, lights or a small fan
Up to 200 W of solar input is generous at this size
Charges to 80% in about 45 minutes
cons: 288 Wh covers only a few laptop charges
No battery expansion, and the solar cable is sold separately

products.name: SOLIX C300X DC
products.tagline: A big power bank: USB-C and DC only, no AC outlets.
pros: Lightest model here at 6.4 lb
Two 140 W two-way USB-C ports charge laptops quickly
Built-in pop-out light
cons: No AC outlets, so it can't run a TV, fridge or kettle
Output is capped at 300 W

products.name: SOLIX C800 Plus
products.tagline: A camping-minded 768 Wh with two detachable lights.
pros: Two detachable camping lights are included
Recharges in about 58 minutes
SurgePad covers loads up to 1,600 W
cons: 768 Wh is less than the 1 kWh models at a similar weight
Rated for 3,000 cycles versus 4,000 on Anker's C1000 Gen 2

products.name: Delta 2
products.tagline: The expandable one: grow it to 3,040 Wh with extra batteries.
pros: Add a Delta 2 or Delta Max battery to reach 2,048 or 3,040 Wh
Up to 500 W of solar input
Four AC outlets at 1,800 W total
cons: At 27 lb, heavier than the Jackery, Anker and Bluetti 1 kWh models
Older 2022 design, rated for 3,000 cycles versus 4,000 on the newer 1 kWh models

products.name: SOLIX C1000 Gen 2
pros: Most output of the group at 2,000 W
Full recharge in 49 minutes at 1,600 W
UPS switchover under 10 ms and 4,000 cycles
cons: Top charging speed has to be enabled in the Anker app
Costs more per watt-hour than the Jackery

products.name: Delta 3 Plus
products.tagline: The Delta 2 successor, with two solar inputs and a quicker recharge.
pros: Takes up to 1,000 W of solar through two inputs
Expands to 5 kWh with compatible EcoFlow batteries
UPS switchover under 10 ms
cons: At 27.6 lb, heavier than the Jackery, Anker and Bluetti 1 kWh models
List price is $300 above the Bluetti Elite 100 V2

products.name: Elite 100 V2
products.tagline: A 25 lb, 1 kWh station at a budget price.
pros: 1,800 W output at a $499 list price
Charges to 80% in about 45 minutes
Takes up to 1,000 W of solar input
cons: 1,024 Wh drains quickly under high-draw loads, as TechRadar noted
Not waterproof, according to Bluetti

products.name: Explorer 1000 v2
products.tagline: A 1 kWh station that stays under 24 lb.
products.ac_charge: About 1 hour with app emergency mode
pros: Lightest of the 1 kWh models here
4,000-cycle LiFePO4 battery
UPS function keeps a fridge or router running through outages
cons: 1,500 W output is the lowest of the 1 kWh group
Fast charging has to be switched on in the app

products.name: Explorer 2000 Plus
products.tagline: 2 kWh and 3,000 W, expandable up to 12 kWh.
pros: 3,000 W continuous with 6,000 W surge
Add up to five battery packs to reach 12 kWh
Two units can be paralleled for 6 kW
cons: At 61.5 lb, the heaviest of the 2 kWh models
Jackery has since released a 2000 v2

products.name: SOLIX C2000 Gen 2
products.tagline: 2 kWh at 41.7 lb, expandable to 4 kWh.
pros: 2,400 W output with four 20 A outlets and a TT-30 for RVs
Expands to 4,096 Wh with the BP2000 battery
4,000-cycle battery and under-10 ms UPS switchover
cons: 41.7 lb is a real lift to carry far
The expansion battery is sold separately

products.name: Elite 200 V2
products.tagline: 2 kWh and 2,600 W with a 6,000-cycle battery.
pros: 6,000 rated cycles, the most here
2,600 W output, up to 3,900 W in power-lifting mode
Charges to 80% in about 1.1 hours
cons: At 53.4 lb, 12 lb heavier than Anker's C2000 Gen 2
Launched at $1,099 and has been discounted since, so the list price here is high

products.name: Delta Pro 3
products.tagline: 4 kWh and 4,000 W for backing up a home's essentials.
pros: 4,000 W output at 120 or 240 V
Expands to 12 kWh with two extra batteries
Takes up to 2,600 W of solar input
cons: At 113.5 lb, you will want the wheels and handle
List price is several times that of a 1 kWh station
